executiveSummary: GM1667 passes the deterministic model contract across all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. The 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, population of 13,653, density of 175 per square kilometre, 23.5% age-65-plus share, eleven neighbourhoods, four BAG places, fifteen BRT settlements and two NWB-derived Dutch logical road links are coherent. Release is nevertheless correction-required for three high-severity spatial defects. The Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset assigns sustained direct municipality inundation stress of 2.2654 from T+12 through T+72, even though the official local stress test excludes inundation from primary and regional defences and instead identifies stream-valley, pluvial and groundwater mechanisms. It produces 6,802 modeled people under pressure and 473,320 cumulative essential-service person-hours at T+72. Nine unrelated nonzero hazards also reuse one exact eleven-neighbourhood ordering. In a controlled T+24 wildfire sourced in the Reuselse Moeren vicinity, the containing southern neighbourhood ranks ninth while neighbourhoods 5.14 and 9.96 kilometres away rank first and second. Local evidence further establishes real pluvial bottlenecks, drought restrictions, cross-municipal wastewater treatment at RWZI Hapert, Dutch-Belgian mobility, external acute-care dependence and utility-provider responsibilities, but none supplies live operational topology or causally changes the simulation. Public-register and current-context layers remain explicitly non-causal; no missing observation is interpreted as normal service, no registered school as a shelter, and no provider territory as physical topology.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 and Gemeente gegeneraliseerd 2025 — GM1667
supports: Machine-readable official identity and annual statistics for GM1667/Reusel-De Mierden: 13,653 residents, density 175 per square kilometre, 23.5% aged 65 or older and 1,802 one-person households.
The companion PDOK OGC API at https://api.pdok.nl/cbs/gebiedsindelingen/ogc/v1 supplies CC BY 4.0 generalized municipality, district and neighbourhood polygons dated 2025-07-01.
BAG place and BRT settlement context comes from the official PDOK registers; administrative boundaries and label points are not hazard, catchment, provider or incident footprints.

CBS neighbourhood values are independently rounded or suppressed, so nulls and a small municipality-to-neighbourhood reconciliation difference are publication semantics rather than measured discrepancies.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Reusel-De Mierden / Provincie Noord-Brabant climate-adaptation portal
evidenceSources.title: Klimaatstresstest gemeente Reusel-De Mierden
supports: The official local study is a first vulnerability indication for water nuisance, drought, heat and flooding and distinguishes those mechanisms spatially.
It calculates no inundation in GM1667 after failure of regional or primary defences; parts of stream valleys can flood from the regional water system.

It projects heavier extreme rain and identifies locally vulnerable water-nuisance areas, while groundwater may rise more than 35 centimetres in western and south-eastern parts without an expected low-drainage damage signal.

Vegetation drought sensitivity is concentrated especially in the north-west and south; precipitation deficit can increase from 210–270 to 300–330 millimetres, and Reuselse Moeren has the municipality's material subsidence band.
Heat exposure increases from roughly 3–6 to 15–18 tropical days and from days to weeks of warm-night stress; vegetation and paving differentiate heat within the village cores.
This is dated scenario/context evidence, not a current event, probability forecast, licensed native GIS feed or operational restoration estimate.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 and Regionaal Crisisplan 2024–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile 2025–2028 final version 1.0; crisis plan 2024–2027
supports: The regional taxonomy covers high river water, extreme-rain waterlogging, defence failure, wildfire, cold and ice, heat, storm, electricity, gas, telecom, drinking water, wastewater and cyber disruption; taxonomy is not proof of local GM1667 intensity or live state.
The profile says the region's high position prevents direct sea or major-river flood danger, while northern large-river flooding can indirectly block drainage from southern Brabant.
Wildfire consequences depend on vegetation, weather, emergency access and extinguishing water; smoke can spread and electricity disruption can cascade.
Vital-process dependencies are supported directionally, but regional statements about redundancy or typical repair do not establish GM1667 asset state, backup, capacity or restoration time.

The companion adopted crisis plan at https://www.vrbzo.nl/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Regionaal-Crisisplan-definitief-vastgesteld-1.pdf treats an acute crisis as up to about three days, provides continuous monitoring and CoPI/ROT/shared-picture roles, and separates general authority from functional chains.
Regional plans are static governance context, not live staffing, stocks, interventions, warnings or machine-readable incident feeds; no explicit dataset reuse licence is stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap De Dommel / Het Waterschapshuis via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Current abstraction restrictions, Reusel-Zuid, RWZI Hapert and IMWA/DAMO water context
evidenceSources.edition: Current page modified 2026-07-31; machine-readable application snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03
supports: At the audit reference time the live page states that the Reusel-with-Nete catchment has an annual surface-water abstraction ban from 1 April through at least 1 November and that a temporary whole-area ban has applied since 16 July 2026. This is dated operating context, not scenario-clock input.

The Reusel-Zuid page at https://www.dommel.nl/reuselzuid locates the brook valley between Hooge Mierde and Reusel west of N269 and describes a 2025–2027 hydrological study to retain water in drought and create room during wet periods; planned design is not completed capacity.

The RWZI page at https://www.dommel.nl/rioolwaterzuivering-hapert states that the treatment plant outside GM1667 serves Bladel and Reusel-De Mierden, handling about 12,200 cubic metres daily and up to 60,000 cubic metres per day during extreme rain.

The current HWH OGC collections at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 and https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 place 101 realized weirs, two surface-water pumps and four sewer pumps in the generalized GM1667 boundary.

HWH object APIs are CC BY-SA 4.0, but contributor completeness varies. Object presence and design figures do not establish hydraulic or sewer connectivity, units for every attribute, control logic, live status, emergency power or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: Water nuisance guidance and work on water storage at Kleine Hoeven I
supports: The municipality records that Kleine Hoeven I water storage did not meet requirements: existing wadis were too shallow and drains were prone to blockage, causing nuisance during heavy rain.

Work beginning 22 June 2026 was planned for six weeks and included deepening storage from 75 to 100 centimetres and raising a dike; completion and resulting operational performance were not verified at the audit reference time.

The companion guidance at https://www.reuseldemierden.nl/wateroverlast says full ditches and high groundwater recur almost annually and sewers cannot always process extreme rainfall, with streets, toilets and manholes affected.

The Lage Mierde disconnection guidance at https://www.reuseldemierden.nl/veelgestelde-vragen-watervergunning-afkoppelen-lage-mierde says a separated system still cannot always process intense summer rain and water on streets remains possible.

These pages establish local mechanisms and a dated project, not a live incident, completion certificate, hydraulic footprint, sewer telemetry or remaining capacity. No explicit dataset reuse licence or fixed update cadence is stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Zuidoost / De Kempen municipalities / Staatsbosbeheer
evidenceSources.title: Joint wildfire management in De Kempen
supports: Reusel-De Mierden, Bladel, Eersel and Bergeijk signed a shared wildfire-management plan with VRBZO and Staatsbosbeheer.
Named measures include replacing conifers with deciduous trees, wetting nature areas and improving emergency-service access, confirming that fuel, moisture and access are spatial determinants.

Staatsbosbeheer's companion Kempen access page at https://www.staatsbosbeheer.nl/uit-in-de-natuur/locaties/kempen/toegankelijkheid identifies Reuselse Moeren within the roughly 2,200-hectare Kempen nature landscape and records cross-border recreational context.

The sources are preparedness and land-use context, not an ignition, perimeter, current fuel-moisture measurement, visitor count, appliance location, crew availability or suppression result; no reusable operational feed is stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Noord-Brabant / Gemeente Reusel-De Mierden / Provincie Antwerpen
evidenceSources.title: NWB, N284 and Dutch-Belgian mobility context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB geometry snapshot 2026-08-01; current project and timetable pages accessed 2026-09-03
supports: NWB provides machine-readable road geometry under CC0 1.0 with monthly updates. The generated municipality graph has only N284 to Bladel and N269 to Hilvarenbeek, each as a logical proxy.

The provincial project page at https://www.brabant.nl/onderwerpen/verkeer-vervoer/wegen-infraprojecten-brabant/n284-reusel-bladel-hapert/ identifies N284 Reusel–Bladel–Hapert as an important route to Eindhoven and A67 and documents congestion, accessibility and safety work.

The municipality's current public-transport page at https://www.reuseldemierden.nl/openbaar-vervoer lists bus 143 to Tilburg, 319 to Eindhoven, neighbourhood bus 291 and hourly De Lijn 43a from Reusel via Arendonk to Turnhout.

The Province of Antwerp start memorandum at https://www.provincieantwerpen.be/content/dam/provant/drem/dienst-ruimtelijke-planning/arendonk---militair-domein/PRUP%20Militair%20Domein_20230411_Startnota.pdf identifies N139 as the Arendonk–Reusel border connection.

Static geometry, project plans and registered transit do not establish live closure, congestion, timetable execution, emergency access, evacuation throughput, Belgian mutual-aid travel or physical utility capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: RIVM / DUO / RDI / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / KNMI / NDW
evidenceSources.title: Official machine-readable care, education, antenna, provider, capacity, weather and road-state context
supports: RIVM version 1.1 acute-care data, published 2026-07-03 under CC0 1.0 on an annual cycle, places no acute hospital in GM1667. Straight-line reference-point distances are 18.806 kilometres to ETZ Tilburg, 19.854 to Máxima MC Veldhoven and 25.331 to Catharina Eindhoven; these are not ambulance travel times or live acceptance.

DUO RIO at https://onderwijsdata.duo.nl/dataset/c416acd1-e083-4ec6-9203-3b20f98fe143 supplies six registered primary-school locations under attribution terms; registered educational use is not shelter designation, capacity, opening, staffing or backup.

The RDI Antenneregister at https://www.rdi.nl/onderwerpen/telecommunicatie/antennes-en-antenneregister contributes 38 antenna-installation records, but not coverage, capacity, backhaul, power backup, outage or operator restoration state.

A live point query to Stichting Mijn Aansluiting's public WMS documented at https://wiki.service.mijnaansluiting.nl/wiki/spaces/Wiki/pages/693731329 returns Enexis for power and gas, Brabant Water for drinking water and Ziggo for fixed media; sewer returns no published match. Territories are Public Domain responsibility context, not topology or service state.

The Netbeheer Nederland capacity-map sample at https://data.partnersinenergie.nl/capaciteitskaart/totaal/afname is large-user planning context at one public postcode, not an outage, feeder, transformer, customer connection or municipality-wide capacity measurement.

The current NDW snapshot contains no matched GM1667 situation and current KNMI/RWS views are scenario-independent context. No match means Unknown/NoData, never an open road, normal utility service, absent hazard or safe facility.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative public context identifies water assets, providers, facilities, external care, wildfire planning and crisis roles, but not live operational capability.
notes: The local water snapshot contributes 101 weirs, two surface-water pumps and four sewer pumps; RWZI Hapert supplies a real cross-municipal wastewater dependency. Neither object presence nor design throughput is live capability.

Provider lookup returns Enexis, Brabant Water and Ziggo at the reference point, with no sewer polygon. These non-causal territories do not establish assets, switching, redundancy, backup or restoration.
Six primary-school and 38 antenna-installation records are registry context, not shelter, coverage, capacity or operational state.
No RIVM acute hospital lies in GM1667; the closest sampled 24/7 emergency departments are external, and straight-line distances are not dispatch or travel estimates.
No sensitive topology, live utility/facility state, priority customers, water-control state, stocks, crews, mutual-aid availability or restoration commitment was inferred.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets completed at every required checkpoint for every essential service, with scenario scope and non-observational semantics recorded.
notes: At T+24: storm severity 0.0421/474 affected; pluvial 0.2087/791; river 0.7096/6,359; coastal 0.0551/zero; heat 0.1042/925; winter 0.6250/2,174; cyber 0.4410/3,399; earthquake ground motion zero; canonical remote wildfire direct fire zero with smoke 0.2379; and compound 0.8213/6,384.

T+24 cumulative essential-service person-hours are 31,419 storm, 40,136 pluvial, 121,388 river, 13,144 coastal, 40,840 heat, 70,765 winter, 69,045 cyber, 634 earthquake, 19,794 wildfire and 122,708 compound.

Canonical coastal direct inundation and remote-wildfire flame remain zero locally; coastal wind and wildfire smoke can remain nonzero. This does not prove absence of indirect supply impacts or a possible local fire.
The remote Groningen earthquake preset has zero current local ground motion at T+24/T+72. Cyber is a synthetic system disruption, not evidence of an operator incident.
All values are deterministic scenario estimates, not observed weather, water depth, ignition, outage, probability, casualty or restoration data.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, cumulative burden, route bounds, local reconciliation and layer invariance pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1667 pnpm audit:model passed both focused tests over 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services.
Every preset at intensity zero yields exact zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.
Repeated frames are deterministic; values are finite and bounded, cumulative burden is monotonic, and logical-route flow does not exceed effective capacity.
All local views preserve 13,653 allocated residents; compound T+24 population, demand and delivery totals reconcile within 8.88e-16.
Switching among overview, hazard, population and all eight service layers leaves the model frame exactly unchanged.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The generic major-river field contradicts official GM1667 evidence, and a common seed ignores mechanism-specific geography and an explicit wildfire source.
notes: The Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset rises to direct inundation stress 2.2654 at T+12 and keeps it through T+72, while E02 excludes defence-breach inundation and E03 excludes direct major-river danger.
River T+24 has severity 0.7096, system pressure 0.4706, 6,359 affected and 121,388 cumulative person-hours; T+72 still has severity 0.7096, pressure 0.4936, 6,802 affected and 473,320 person-hours.

Nine unrelated nonzero presets share the exact neighbourhood rank BU16670008, BU16670109, BU16670300, BU16670002, BU16670100, BU16670309, BU16670200, BU16670209, BU16670009, BU16670000, BU16670001. Official evidence differentiates stream valleys, pluvial bottlenecks, paving/vegetation, network targets and nature-fire landscape.

A diagnostic T+24 wildfire sourced at [5.1524, 51.3171] in the Reuselse Moeren vicinity gives municipality direct fire 0.3787, smoke 0.5010 and severity 0.4290. The containing BU16670009 ranks 9/11; BU16670008 5.136 kilometres away ranks first and BU16670109 9.963 kilometres away ranks second. The source is synthetic and not an observed incident.
Exact remote-hazard zeros and coincidental local rank agreement cannot validate a spatial allocation that samples none of the cited mechanism surfaces.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances and dependency ledgers are inspectable, but their magnitudes are not calibrated to GM1667 water, utility, care, supply or cross-border networks.
notes: River T+72 availability is lowest for drainage 0.2929, facilities 0.3304, telecom 0.4058 and water 0.4094; these are unsupported consequences of unsupported river forcing.
Compound T+24 availability is telecom 0.2512, drainage 0.3567 and water 0.3966; the public sources support dependency directions but do not calibrate these exact values.

The causal graph has no named Enexis feeder/station, Brabant Water pressure zone, municipal sewer catchment/control, RDI operator/backhaul, RWZI Hapert edge, external hospital transfer, shelter, depot, retail stock or Belgian support node.
All eight service views reuse road-derived links and 300 nominal scenario units; logical-proxy semantics never turn them into physical utility capacity.
Public-context layers explicitly affectSimulation=false and therefore cannot validate causal topology or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality ledgers close arithmetically and preserve confidence, dependency ordering, controls and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; weighted service contributions sum to municipality system pressure.
Dependency chains, drivers, recovery progress and restoration counterfactuals are finite and inspectable.
Preparedness changes modeled consequences after physical pressure rather than changing physical hazard fragility.
Interventions are labeled scenario assumptions and route flows remain logical proxies.
Cumulative essential-service person-hours are a matched no-event proxy, not observed outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.

recovery72h.summary: Time gates and persistence are deterministic, but unsupported forcing and missing operational resources prevent a local first-72-hour recovery interpretation.
notes: Unsupported river forcing remains active through T+72 with 6,802 affected and 473,320 cumulative person-hours; this is not a De Dommel or crisis-team forecast.
Pluvial current hazard clears by T+72 while cumulative burden reaches 84,222; compound retains flood stress 0.2988 and cyber 0.0591, with pressure 0.4985, 6,897 affected and 462,141 person-hours.

The heatwave retains temperature 25.30 degrees Celsius and drought 0.5789 at T+72 while thresholded affectedPopulation is zero; that output must not be read as absence of residual health, care, water-demand or agricultural burden.

E03 supports monitoring, CoPI/ROT/shared-picture work and transition around the three-day horizon, but generic model responseDelayHours and intervention multipliers are not actual decisions or resources.
The active abstraction bans are audit-date operating context only and must expire by source valid time rather than persist in, or be shifted onto, the scenario clock.
Actual water controls, N284/N269/Belgian access, utility switching, hospitals, staff, crews, mutual aid, fuel, spares, stocks and restoration estimates remain Unknown.

findings.summary: A coarse generic corridor creates unsupported sustained direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation across high-ground GM1667.
findings.evidence: E02 calculates no GM1667 inundation from regional or primary-defence failure and instead identifies water-system stream valleys; E03 says Brabant-Zuidoost has no direct major-river flood danger, retaining only indirect blocked-drainage pathways. The model nevertheless emits direct inundation stress 2.2654 from T+12 through T+72. It yields 6,359 modeled people/121,388 cumulative essential-service person-hours at T+24 and 6,802/473,320 at T+72. No connected footprint, defence scenario, backwater model, level, arrival, duration or depth supports this output.
findings.action: Make the named-major-river direct forcing for GM1667 numerically neutral and explicitly Unsupported/Unknown until an expert-selected versioned hydraulic footprint establishes a connection. Preserve Reusel brook, groundwater, pluvial and indirect blocked-drainage mechanisms as unresolved rather than safe.

findings.summary: Nine unrelated hazards reuse one exact neighbourhood rank instead of GM1667's mapped water, heat, land-cover and network mechanisms.
findings.evidence: E02 differentiates water-system flooding, pluvial nuisance, groundwater, drought and heat; E05 supplies a specific wadi/drain bottleneck; E06 makes fuel, moisture and access spatial determinants. Despite that, every nonzero storm, pluvial, river, coastal-wind, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound T+24 map has the identical exact order of all eleven neighbourhoods beginning BU16670008, BU16670109 and BU16670300. The allocation samples no hydraulic cell, elevation, pavement/vegetation, network target, exposed road or fuel surface.
findings.action: Label current neighbourhood ranks synthetic/unsupported and prohibit operational prioritisation from them. Replace the shared seed with separately versioned and licensed mechanism inputs, preserving resolution, event definition, units, edition, no-data and validation metadata.

findings.summary: An explicit source in the Reuselse Moeren nature landscape does not control the direct-fire neighbourhood map.
findings.evidence: E02 locates important vegetation drought sensitivity in southern GM1667 and E06 documents Reuselse Moeren and spatial wildfire measures. In a reproducible synthetic T+24 test, source [5.1524, 51.3171] lies in CBS BU16670009 and produces municipality fire 0.3787, smoke 0.5010 and severity 0.4290. The containing neighbourhood ranks 9/11 at 0.3786, while BU16670008 5.136 kilometres away and BU16670109 9.963 kilometres away rank first and second. This proves source blindness; it is not evidence of an actual fire.
findings.action: Until source/perimeter-aware allocation exists, mark neighbourhood flame ranks unsupported. Prefer an authorized NIPV wildfire-risk export; otherwise combine eligible BRT/TOP10NL land cover, an explicit ignition/perimeter and timestamped KNMI weather with inspectable fuel, wind, access, extinguishing-water and suppression assumptions.

findings.summary: Real local water bottlenecks and cross-municipal wastewater dependence are displayed as context but absent from causal drainage and recovery.
findings.evidence: E04 supplies 101 weirs, two surface-water pumps, four sewer pumps, Reusel-Zuid study context, an active drought restriction and dependence on RWZI Hapert. E05 documents shallow wadis, blockage-prone drains and residual separated-sewer limits. Yet the T+24 pluvial drainage availability 0.6017 and all recovery values are generic; assets have no typed connectivity, capacity units, controls, power dependence or live state and affectSimulation=false.
findings.action: Build an authorized, versioned catchment/sewer dependency layer with typed asset function and explicit Unknown for topology, control, backup and state. Keep public objects non-causal until validated; test Kleine Hoeven/Lage Mierde wet pathways and RWZI Hapert loss without interpreting missing records as zero.

findings.summary: The two-link municipality graph omits the Belgian N139 and cross-border transit, evacuation, supply and mutual-aid continuity.
findings.evidence: E07 identifies the N284/A67 and N269/Tilburg axes, the N139 Reusel–Arendonk connection and hourly De Lijn 43a to Arendonk/Turnhout. The generated graph contains only N284 to Bladel and N269 to Hilvarenbeek, both logical proxies totaling 300 nominal units, while its 25 stop areas have no route or timetable semantics. There is no foreign gateway, border status, detour, emergency-access or Belgian mutual-aid edge.
findings.action: Add separately typed, source-versioned Dutch and Flemish road/transit gateway continuity. Apply it only to eligible mobility, supply, evacuation and mutual-aid analyses, retain live closure/timetable as Unknown without feeds, and never clone road capacity into utility services.

findings.summary: Provider responsibility is known, but physical utility topology, operational state, backup and repair capability are not public model inputs.
findings.evidence: E08's live public point lookup returns Enexis for power/gas, Brabant Water for water and Ziggo for fixed media; sewer has no match. It also supplies one large-user capacity-planning sample and 38 antenna records. None establishes feeder/pressure/backhaul/sewer topology, customer connectivity, switching, redundancy, incident state, priority sites, backup endurance, crews, spares or restoration. Exact service values therefore remain synthetic.
findings.action: Keep responsibility polygons, antenna registers and planning samples visibly non-causal. Obtain operator-authorized aggregated topology/state interfaces with valid time, licence and security review; otherwise expose each missing property as Unknown and suppress provider-specific restoration claims.

findings.summary: A resident-only denominator and generic facility service omit transient populations, care dependency and external acute-care access.
findings.evidence: E01 reports 23.5% age 65 or older across four village cores and dispersed rural areas. E08 finds no acute hospital inside GM1667, with straight-line reference distances of 18.806 kilometres to ETZ Tilburg and 19.854 to Máxima MC Veldhoven, and six local primary schools that are not shelters. E06/E07 establish recreation and Belgian movement, but no live tourist, worker, shopper, event, school-day, home-care, bed, occupancy, acceptance or ambulance data are present.
findings.action: Label affectedPopulation as a CBS-resident estimate. Add only privacy-preserving, date-valid visitor/commuter/event and care-vulnerability ranges; represent external hospital routes and live acceptance separately, and never infer shelter or clinical capacity from registry class.

findings.summary: Generic delays and intervention multipliers are not GM1667 first-72-hour actions, resources or restoration commitments.
findings.evidence: E03 defines continuous monitoring, CoPI/ROT/shared-picture roles, distinct general and functional-chain authority, and transition from an acute roughly three-day crisis. It does not provide exact staffing, stocks, pumps, crews, mutual aid, intervention timing or provider repair rates. Model responseDelayHours, controls and restoration counterfactuals are transparent assumptions but cannot be attributed to the municipality, water board, safety region or operators.
findings.action: In the UI separate scenario controls, planned/authorized actions, observed execution and operator forecasts. For each 0–72-hour action show owner, authority, evidence/valid time, prerequisite, resource, dependency and Unknown state; do not convert a regional role description into an automatic effect.

findings.summary: Current/register context requires explicit valid-time and NoData semantics and must remain independent of scenario time.
findings.evidence: E04's current page, modified 31 July 2026 and checked 3 September, says the Reusel seasonal ban runs 1 April to at least 1 November and a whole-area temporary ban has applied since 16 July; its expiry remains source-controlled. E08's NDW snapshot has no GM1667 match, while RIVM, DUO, RDI, provider and capacity sources have differing cadences and meanings. A missing road, sewer-provider, water-gauge, warning or event record is NoData/Unknown, never evidence of normal operation or absence.
findings.action: Display publisher, retrieval time, observation/issue/expiry time, cadence, licence, coverage and affectsSimulation for every context layer. Expire live restrictions and observations by source rules, never advance them with the scenario clock, and render empty/no-match as Unknown/NoData rather than zero or green.

findings.summary: The generated identity, editions, nulls and rounded neighbourhood reconciliation are internally coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 matches GM1667/Reusel-De Mierden, province, 2025 statistics and boundary. The bundle retains all eleven official neighbourhoods, four BAG places and fifteen BRT settlements; no place centre lies outside the generalized boundary. Neighbourhood population differs by only +7 (+0.051%) from the independently rounded municipality row. District heating and public charging remain null for all neighbourhoods rather than fabricated.
findings.action: Preserve source, licence, edition, null and reconciliation metadata and re-run the same checks after every CBS/PDOK refresh.

findings.summary: The focused full-matrix model contract passes determinism, bounds, exact-zero, reconciliation, causal closure and layer-invariance checks.
findings.evidence: The focused audit executed ten presets at six checkpoints over eight services.
